subject: aviation-maintenance
intro: Aviation maintenance leads to the professions that keep aircraft airworthy: A and P mechanics overhauling engines and airframes, avionics specialists wiring flight decks, and test technicians supporting aerospace engineering teams.

roles.title: Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians
roles.what: Diagnose, adjust, repair and overhaul aircraft engines and assemblies such as hydraulic and pneumatic systems, following FAA standards, inspection schedules and maintenance records to return aircraft to service safely.
roles.where: This course is the FAA Part 147 curriculum itself — airframe systems, powerplant units on reciprocating and turbine engines, and the inspection and airworthiness unit on annuals, 100-hour checks, ADs and return to service.

roles.title: Avionics Technicians
roles.what: Install, inspect, test, adjust and repair avionics equipment — radar, radio and navigation systems — in aircraft and space vehicles, tracing faults through complex integrated electronics.
roles.where: The aircraft electrical and instruments unit — aircraft electrical systems, avionics and instrument systems, communication and navigation — is precisely the equipment set avionics technicians own.

roles.title: Aerospace Engineering and Operations Technologists and Technicians
roles.what: Install, run and maintain the equipment used to develop, test, produce and sustain aircraft and spacecraft, performing systems readiness tests and pre- and post-operational checkouts under simulated conditions.
roles.where: The general unit's aircraft drawings, maths and physics for aviation maintenance build the measurement and test discipline this role uses, and airframe systems knowledge grounds the checkout work.
